input.question: besides the dollar amount, what the hell are autioneers actually saying?
input.ground_truth: It doesn't really matter what they're saying. The point is to get you psyched up and excited so you're more prone to buying something. All about energy levels moreso than actual content. If you go to some auctions for more expensive items (luxury cars, art, etc.), then you'll probably hear a slower auctioneer and a more thorough description of the item.

Question: besides the dollar amount, what the hell are autioneers actually saying?

response.prediction:
Okay, let’s imagine you and your friend are playing a game where you both want the same toy, but there’s only one. So, you decide to take turns saying bigger and bigger numbers to see who wants the toy the most.

At an auction, people are doing something kind of like that. When the auctioneer is talking really fast and saying numbers, they are asking, “How much do you want this thing?” Each time someone says “I want it for this much money!” and the auctioneer keeps asking, “Is that the most anyone will pay?” They keep going until no one wants to pay more, and then the toy (or whatever is being sold) goes to the person who offered the biggest number.

So, besides the numbers (the dollar amount), the auctioneer is really just asking, “Who wants it more?” and making sure everyone gets a chance to say how much they want it. They’re also making sure everyone is following the rules of the game.
